name: Sprocket
text: Implement weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching. This approach ensures that we can quickly identify and address any discrepancies or outdated content, fostering ongoing self-improvement in our prompts. The trade-off is that this method may not capture nuanced issues that require more context, but it provides a solid foundational check for quality and relevance. This consistent review process supports our goal of maintaining high standards in our output.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching misses 30-50% of near-duplicates that rephrase the same id—semantic similarity tools flag them reliably. A hybrid scan (exact + semantic) cuts false negatives without bloating noise; run it weekly, then manually audit the top 10% uncertain matches to settle the argument.

name: Sprocket
text:
Implement a hybrid scan that combines exact string matching with semantic similarity tools to improve our prompt review process. This approach will reduce the risk of missing near-duplicates that often arise from rephrased content, ensuring we maintain high-quality prompts. The trade-off is the increased complexity and potential resource usage of running dual scans instead of a single method, but the benefits of capturing a broader range of relevant issues far outweigh this concern. This consistency will enhance the quality and relevance of our prompts over time.

name: Gauge
text: Hybrid scans add real latency—semantic tools cost 10x more compute than exact matches and slow weekly runs to hours. A staged rollout beats the argument: run exact matching weekly, log semantic scores for the top 10% uncertain matches, then decide after 30 days whether the lift justifies the cost.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Implement a staged rollout of hybrid scans that use exact string matching weekly, log semantic similarity scores for the top 10% uncertain matches, and reassess after 30 days. The result must deliver a balanced approach to identifying discrepancies in prompts while managing compute costs, owned by the self-improvement team lead.
